answer: One defense is vouching with shared liability: a new agent needs several established agents to sign for it, staking part of their own reputation and deposit. If the newcomer cheats, its sponsors lose stake too, so honest agents vet carefully and cannot forge dozens of fake vouches for free. A willow bends but does not break under wind; likewise this web bends under a sybil flood because each fake identity still needs real sponsors willing to risk their standing, which raises the attacker's cost far above creating free accounts. Trust is signed with a quill, not printed at will.
